headline: Your first real customer
body: A lead from your network just signed a real contract. Not a friend doing you a favour — an actual paying customer.

options.label: Celebrate properly
options.detail: Take the team out and mark the moment before getting back to work tomorrow.

options.label: Reinvest every cent
options.detail: Skip the celebration and put the money straight back into the product.
options.storyHeadline: Put the first revenue straight back into the product

headline: {MENTOR} calls, unprompted
body: She's heard how things are going and has opinions about your strategy that she didn't wait to be asked for.

options.label: Listen carefully
options.detail: Take detailed notes and actually weigh what she's saying.
options.storyHeadline: Took a mentor's advice to heart

options.label: Push back politely
options.detail: Hear her out, then explain why you're sticking with your own read on this.

headline: Great engineer wants in
body: Someone you respect is interested in joining as employee #2. They want 5% equity.

options.label: Hire for cash + 2%
options.detail: Negotiate them down to 2% equity plus a bigger cash number today.
options.mentorHint: You save equity today. They know what the fair offer was, and they'll remember who didn't make it.

options.label: Give them what they want
options.detail: The full 5% equity they asked for, at market rate.
options.storyHeadline: First hire joins at fair terms
options.mentorHint: Market rate costs more equity now, permanently, in every future cap table calculation.

options.label: Can't afford it yet
options.detail: Tell them honestly and hope they're still available when you can.
options.mentorHint: Nothing costs anything today. Someone this good doesn't usually wait around to be affordable.

headline: Customers want a feature you didn't plan
body: Multiple paying customers request the same capability. Building it would delay other work.

options.label: Build what customers want
options.detail: Drop what's next in line and build the feature they're actually asking for.
options.mentorHint: Customers get what they asked for. Everything else on the roadmap quietly slips behind it.

options.label: Stick to your roadmap
options.detail: Explain the vision and hold the line — the feature stays unbuilt for now.
options.mentorHint: You keep the roadmap intact. The customers who asked notice you didn't build it for them.

headline: A rival launches, funded at $20M
body: A well-financed newcomer enters your market and starts undercutting you on price.

options.label: Compete on product, not price
options.detail: Ignore their pricing and double down on what only you do well.

options.label: Sidestep into an adjacent market
options.detail: Skip the price war entirely and find customers they haven't reached yet.

headline: The customer who wants it built their way
body: A big customer will sign if you build three things only they need.

options.label: Build it
options.detail: Six months of engineering you'll probably regret.
options.storyHeadline: Bent the roadmap for one customer
options.mentorHint: Six months of engineering for one customer. You'll find out whether it was worth it long after you've already spent it.

options.label: Say no politely
options.detail: They walk, you stay clean.
options.mentorHint: They walk, and you stay clean. You also don't get to know what that contract would have become.

options.label: Build one of the three
options.detail: They're half happy. So are you.
options.mentorHint: They're half happy. You've now built a third of a feature you may end up finishing anyway.

headline: Everyone is asking for the same missing thing
body: Forty customers have now asked for the same feature. Your team thinks it's boring.

options.label: Build it
options.detail: Engineers grumble. Customers stop asking.
options.mentorHint: Customers stop asking. Your engineers remember exactly whose idea this was.

options.label: Build what's exciting instead
options.detail: Morale is up. Customers quietly leave.
options.mentorHint: Morale's up in the building. The forty people who asked are quietly starting to look elsewhere.

headline: Your prices are too low
body: Nobody has ever said no because of the price. That's usually a sign.

options.label: Raise prices 30%
options.detail: Lose 8% of customers, keep the rest at a better price.
options.mentorHint: You lose 8% of customers on purpose. You won't know which 8% until they're already gone.

options.label: Raise them for new customers only
options.detail: No complaints from anyone already in.
options.storyHeadline: Quietly raised prices for new signups
options.mentorHint: No complaints from anyone already in — and a two-tier price list you'll be explaining for years.

options.label: Leave them
options.detail: Nothing changes, forever.
options.mentorHint: Nothing changes today. Nothing changes tomorrow either, which is exactly the problem.

headline: One customer is a third of your revenue
body: If they leave, you're in serious trouble. They know this.

options.label: Spend a year chasing smaller customers
options.detail: Growth slows. You sleep better.
options.storyHeadline: Diversified away from one big customer

options.label: Go even deeper with them
options.detail: They practically own you now.
options.storyHeadline: Went all-in on the biggest customer

headline: A customer won't pay
body: Four months late. They keep saying next week.

options.label: Cut them off
options.detail: Lose the revenue. Others notice you're serious.
options.storyHeadline: Cut off a customer who wouldn't pay
options.mentorHint: You lose the revenue today. Everyone watching learns you're serious, including the customers who pay on time.

options.label: Keep serving them and hope
options.detail: A coin flip on whether they ever pay.
options.storyHeadline: Kept a non-paying customer, for now

gamble.winText: They finally paid, in full, with an apology.
gamble.loseText: They never paid. You should have known.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: The late payer finally paid up
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Wrote off a customer who never paid

options.label: Offer a payment plan
options.detail: You get most of it, slowly.
options.storyHeadline: Put a non-payer on a payment plan
options.mentorHint: You get most of it, slowly — and you've just taught them that not paying gets them a better deal.

headline: The customers you have are the wrong ones
body: They're small, difficult and don't pay much. The good ones are somewhere else.

options.label: Stop selling to them, start again upmarket
options.detail: Painful now, much better later.
options.storyHeadline: Walked away from the wrong customers

options.label: Keep them, they're paying
options.detail: Safe. Capped. Forever.
options.storyHeadline: Kept the customers who were easy to keep

headline: Support is drowning
body: Every question comes to two people and both are exhausted.

options.label: Hire two more
options.detail: Costs go up. Morale recovers fast.
options.storyHeadline: Hired to fix the support backlog

options.label: Write help pages and hope
options.detail: Half the questions stop. Half don't.

options.label: Do nothing
options.detail: Someone quits.
options.storyHeadline: Let the support backlog burn people out

headline: Simple or powerful
body: Your customers want more features. New customers find it confusing already.

options.label: Add the features
options.detail: Existing customers happy, new signups slower.
options.storyHeadline: Added the features customers asked for
options.mentorHint: Existing customers stay happy. New signups take longer to convince, quietly, for a while.

options.label: Strip it back
options.detail: New signups jump. A dozen loyal customers are furious.
options.mentorHint: New signups jump. The loyal customers furious about it were also your best word of mouth.

headline: Build it or buy it
body: You could buy a small tool that does part of the job, or spend six months building it.

options.label: Buy it
options.detail: Working next month.
options.mentorHint: Working next month. You'll be paying for someone else's roadmap for as long as you use it.

options.label: Build it
options.detail: Six months of work. Better. Yours.
options.storyHeadline: Built it in-house, the slow way
options.mentorHint: Six months of work you can't spend building anything else, for something a tool already does.

headline: The feature nobody uses
body: Eleven percent of the product is used by 0.3% of customers. It costs a fortune to maintain.

options.label: Delete it
options.detail: Costs down. A handful of very angry emails.
options.storyHeadline: Cut a feature almost nobody used
options.mentorHint: Costs come down today. The handful of angry emails are from the customers who cared enough to write one.

options.label: Keep it
options.detail: Nothing changes. Everything is slower.
options.storyHeadline: Kept maintaining a feature nobody uses
options.mentorHint: Nothing changes today. It keeps costing you the same fortune tomorrow, and the day after.

headline: The product is too slow
body: Customers don't complain. They just use it less.

options.label: Spend a quarter fixing speed
options.detail: Nothing visible ships. Usage climbs.
options.storyHeadline: Spent a quarter on nothing but speed

options.label: Ship new features instead
options.detail: Usage keeps sliding.
options.storyHeadline: Shipped features instead of fixing speed

headline: Should it be free to try?
body: Right now people have to pay before they see it.

options.label: Free trial
options.detail: Way more signups, worth less per customer.
options.mentorHint: Way more signups. Each one is worth less, and you won't know how much less until you add it up later.

options.label: Keep the paywall
options.detail: Fewer, better customers.
options.storyHeadline: Kept the product behind a paywall
options.mentorHint: Fewer, better customers — and a much smaller number of people ever finding out you exist.

headline: Your first real manager
body: You can't be in every conversation any more.

options.label: Hire an experienced one from outside
options.detail: Costs more. Some resentment. It works.

options.label: Promote someone loyal
options.detail: Cheap. They might be out of their depth.

gamble.winText: They grew into it faster than anyone expected.
gamble.loseText: They were out of their depth, and everyone could see it.

headline: Cheap and eager or expensive and proven
body: Two candidates. One costs three times the other.

options.label: The expensive one
options.detail: Output jumps immediately.
options.storyHeadline: Paid up for a proven hire
options.mentorHint: Output jumps now. That's cash you can't spend twice, whether or not they're still here in a year.

options.label: The cheap one
options.detail: Slower, loyal, might be brilliant in two years.
options.storyHeadline: Bet on a cheaper, unproven hire
options.mentorHint: Cheaper today. 'Might be brilliant in two years' is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

headline: Everyone wants a pay rise
body: Not unreasonably.

options.label: Give it
options.detail: Costs go up. Morale is much better.

options.label: Say not yet
options.detail: Morale drops. Two people start looking.

headline: A rival is hiring your people
body: {RIVAL} has been calling your team.

options.label: Match their offers
options.detail: Costs rise across the board.
options.storyHeadline: Matched a rival's offers to keep the team

options.label: Let whoever wants to go, go
options.detail: Two leave. The rest are committed.
options.storyHeadline: Let the door swing both ways

headline: Do you need an office at all?
body: The lease is up.

options.label: Take a bigger one
options.detail: The team likes it. It costs more.
options.mentorHint: The team likes it. That's real money leaving every month whether or not the team's actually bigger.

options.label: Go fully remote
options.detail: Cheaper. New people take longer to fit in.
options.mentorHint: Cheaper immediately. New people take longer to actually feel like they're on the team.

headline: Hire a salesperson or sell it yourself
body: You've been doing all the selling.

options.label: Hire one
options.detail: Costs more up front, revenue climbs after.

options.label: Keep doing it yourself
options.detail: Revenue grows slower. You do nothing else.

headline: Cut costs or keep growing
body: You can be safe or you can be fast.

options.label: Cut 15% of spending
options.detail: Growth slows. Cash lasts much longer.

options.label: Keep spending
options.detail: You're betting on the growth showing up in time.

headline: Late payers
body: Everyone pays 60 days late. That's two months of your money sitting elsewhere.

options.label: Charge a fee for late payment
options.detail: Better cash flow. Two customers annoyed.
options.mentorHint: Better cash flow. The two customers you annoyed are the ones who talk to other customers.

options.label: Offer a discount for paying early
options.detail: Cash lasts longer. Revenue is a little lower.
options.storyHeadline: Offered a discount for paying early
options.mentorHint: Cash lasts longer. You've just told every customer that paying late is worth less than paying you at all.

headline: Borrow instead of selling shares
body: A bank will lend against your revenue.

options.label: Take the loan
options.detail: No shares given up. Repayments start immediately.
options.storyHeadline: Took on debt instead of dilution
options.mentorHint: No shares given up. Repayments don't care whether revenue shows up on time.

options.label: Raise from investors
options.detail: No repayments, but you give up equity.
options.mentorHint: No repayments — but the equity's gone even in the years the loan would've been paid off.

headline: Should you write publicly?
body: Everyone says the founder should post about the company.

options.label: Start writing every week
options.detail: Slow burn, real signups over time.
options.mentorHint: Slow burn. Every week you don't write becomes a small, visible admission that you stopped.

options.label: Don't
options.detail: Nothing. And nobody knows who you are.
options.storyHeadline: Decided not to bother with public writing
options.mentorHint: Costs nothing today. Nobody outside your customers will ever know this company exists.

headline: Advertise or not
body: Paid advertising works but it never stops costing.

options.label: Spend on it
options.detail: Signups jump while you pay. Stop paying, stop growing.

options.label: Spend on content instead
options.detail: Slow for a year, then free forever.
options.storyHeadline: Invested in content instead of ads

headline: Write it down or keep it in your head
body: Nobody knows how anything is decided.

options.label: Write the handbook
options.detail: Slower for a week. Clearer forever.

options.label: Keep improvising
options.detail: Fast today. Every new hire takes months to ramp.

headline: A holiday
body: Two weeks, no laptop.

options.label: Go
options.detail: Nothing breaks. The company runs fine without you, which is unsettling.

options.label: Stay
options.detail: You keep working. You keep being tired.

headline: A supplier goes bust owing you nothing
body: They simply vanish. You need a new one by Tuesday.

options.label: Scramble and find a replacement fast
options.detail: Two weeks of chaos, then fine.
options.storyHeadline: Scrambled to replace a vanished supplier

headline: Someone leaves a very long review
body: Two thousand words, mostly positive, deeply strange.

options.label: Reply properly
options.detail: They become an evangelist for a decade.
options.storyHeadline: Replied properly to a strange, long review

options.label: Ignore it
options.detail: Nothing.
